hardDay.heading: Hard day? Start here.
hardDay.body:
Chapter 5 refuses to romanticize pain. Not every struggle is a lesson to rush through. Cry out to God. You're allowed to tell God it hurts. The Psalms do this over and over. Psalm 13 is a good place to start. Ask for help. If you're not safe, get safe first. If someone is hurting you, call 911, or the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-7233.

Your task this week is honesty and one trusted believer. When you can, read "Formation Without Romanticizing Pain."

If you are in danger, or you are having thoughts of not wanting to live, please stop here and reach out now. In the U.S., call or text 988, or call 911. Then tell a pastor or a trusted believer today.

read.heading: Read first: Chapter 5
read.body:
Open to Chapter 5, "Purpose, Not a Perfect Map." Read "Struggle Is Not Always a Detour" and "Tuesday Morning: When the Map Is Still Blank." Then read "I've Lived This Kind of Formation."

In that section I tell you about our blended family, nine kids, and how raising them was not a story of surplus. The skills I lean on today were built in the seasons I felt least ready. Some of what I called "not ready" turned out to be God getting me ready. And I'm clear in the book: that's not a formula.

Read it with your own hard season in mind. Then come back.

pulse.heading: The pulse: light for the next step
pulse.body:
God often gives purpose through the path, not before it. Struggle can be formation, not always a detour.

Chapter 5 changes the question. Stop asking, "Do I see the whole map?" Start asking, "Has God given light for the next step?" Abraham went without the full map. We don't get to demand that God tell us everything as the price of obeying anything.

nameIt.heading: Name it: formation or excuse?
nameIt.body:
There are two ways to walk through a hard season. Formation says, "Father, use this." Excuse says, "This pain means I can ignore what You already said."

Chapter 5 also gives a simple test for waiting. Holy waiting can name the door it's waiting on. Foggy delay can only name the fear.

If you're in fresh grief, illness, or depression, this isn't a test you have to pass this week. Tap "Hard day?" and start there. God is patient with you.

verses.text: Count it all joy, my brothers, when you meet trials of various kinds, for you know that the testing of your faith produces steadfastness. And let steadfastness have its full effect, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing.

Not only that, but we rejoice in our sufferings, knowing that suffering produces endurance, and endurance produces character, and character produces hope, and hope does not put us to shame, because God’s love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us.

build.heading: Build it: three plain duties
build.body:
Start smaller than the big question. Don't ask what you're supposed to do with your whole life. Ask what God has already made plain for today.

Love your family. Do today's work honestly. Tell the truth. Deal with sin quickly. Open your Bible even when you feel flat.

Write three duties that are already plain this week. Then pick one offline act of love to do first.

move.heading: Move: this week's practice
move.body:
From the end of Chapter 5:

Write three "already plain" duties for this week. Complete one offline act of love before you consume more "calling content."

That means before the next video, podcast, or post about purpose. Love first. If the week slips, pick a new date within three days.

help.heading: Help: name a neighbor
help.body:
If you can't name your calling yet, name a neighbor. Jesus summed up the law with love for God and love for neighbor, and that still stands when the map is blank.

Bring one answer to a trusted believer this week. Then ask: who is the neighbor right in front of me? Do one ordinary thing for them.

pray.heading: Pray it: Father, use this
pray.body:
Joseph's path looked like a wrong turn. God was weaving it for good. Ask what He might be forming in you that ease would never teach.

Father, I don't see the whole map. I'm asking for light for the next step.

This hard thing is ____. I'm not asking You to make it pretty. I'm asking You to use it.

Show me today's mile. Help me love ____ well this week. Amen.

review.heading: Review: fruit after first steps
review.body:
After your date, mark it: took the step, not yet, or holy wait.

Fruit grows after obedient first steps, not perfect conditions. That's the pattern in Chapter 5, and it's my story too.

Guardrail, "What This Is Not": this isn't earning. Not every struggle is holy. Planning isn't bad. Feelings aren't the test. And none of this gives you a license to freeze.
